root_cause.text: The smc91x driver’s custom smc_special_trylock() used local_irq_save()+spin_trylock() instead of an RT-safe irqsave spinlock primitive, causing IRQ state to become unbalanced on PREEMPT_RT because smc_special_unlock() used spin_unlock_irqrestore() with different RT semantics.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces the hand-rolled macro `local_irq_save(flags); __ret = spin_trylock(lock); ...` with `spin_trylock_irqsave(lock, flags)`, and the commit/CVE explicitly states that on PREEMPT_RT “smc_special_trylock() disables IRQs even on PREEMPT_RT, but smc_special_unlock() does not restore IRQs on PREEMPT_RT.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace the open-coded smc trylock IRQ-save macro with the standard spin_trylock_irqsave helper.
intent_record.what: The multi-line macro definition of smc_special_trylock(lock, flags), which manually called local_irq_save(flags), spin_trylock(lock), and conditionally local_irq_restore(flags) on failure, was replaced with a single macro expansion to spin_trylock_irqsave(lock, flags).
intent_record.how: At runtime, smc_special_trylock now uses the kernel's standard combined trylock-and-interrupt-save primitive instead of open-coded logic, preserving the same trylock-with-IRQ-save behavior while relying on the canonical implementation for correct lock and interrupt state handling.

candidates.rationale: This open-coded IRQ state save is the core of the bug: it bypasses the RT-safe spin_trylock_irqsave semantics, so the IRQ state saved here does not match the restore behavior later used by smc_special_unlock() on PREEMPT_RT.

Using plain spin_trylock() after local_irq_save() creates a non-atomic, non-RT-safe trylock+irqsave sequence. On PREEMPT_RT this differs semantically from spin_trylock_irqsave and leads to unbalanced IRQ state with the corresponding unlock path.
This macro definition embodies the vulnerable custom locking primitive whose implementation incorrectly combines local_irq_save() and spin_trylock() instead of using the standard RT-safe helper.
